findings.summary: Appending `: <reason>` to every 'not read' line also changes lines that have nothing to do with unread jobs: go errors with no job, budget-stopped reads and no-capability readings.
findings.evidence: `push` formats `drain      {item} → {job} ({outcome})`, and the outcome is 'not read' for every arm of `(_, error, _)` in `run_job`, not only the new Unread case. The plan says the change avoids 'altering lines for other outcomes', but it still alters every existing 'not read' line. Fix: Either print the reason only for the new Unread return, or grep tests/drain.rs and the display tests for `(not read)` before editing, and update any exact-match assertions on purpose. Say which in the plan.
findings.location: Plan decision 5 / drain.rs `push` (line 1039) and the job-None read path in `run_job` (lines 1129-1139)

findings.summary: `athena go` on an unread Proposed job now spends reader budget with no prompt. User-facing text that points to `athena correct` as the way to re-read may now be stale.
findings.evidence: The old bail text at run/mod.rs:332 was the only pointer to `athena correct` for this state. The plan grepped tests, but not CLI help text or docs that describe what `go` does for a Proposed job. Fix: Before editing, grep main.rs help text and docs/ for 'has no reading' and 'correct ... reads it again'. Make sure the main.rs Reread printing shows the reader error when the re-read fails again. Mention the new `go` behavior in the CHANGELOG entry too.
findings.location: Plan Risks, first bullet / Open question 4 (main.rs GoResult::Reread printing)

findings.summary: The criterion says the reader 'returns unparseable output'; the plan's fake returns no structured output.
findings.evidence: A structured reading that does not parse may take the refusal path, which runs the reader twice inside one read. The plan explains this choice in decision 6. Fix: In the test's doc comment, say that 'no structured reading' is the unparseable case used and why, so the verifier does not count it as a gap against the criterion.

findings.summary: A skipped item stays Proposed with no reading, so every later drain will read it twice again.
findings.evidence: Nothing in the plan marks or deprioritises the item after it is skipped. That is within scope, since the reading bounds the re-read per item, not per job. Fix: Optionally have the skip note say the job stays proposed and can be re-read with `athena go <id>` or closed, so the person running drain knows what to do next.

summary: I checked the plan against the snapshot code, reading the files directly. It finds the fault in the places where it actually starts. First, in reading.rs, `first_reading` (lines 826-878) and `correct` (lines 916-1051) commit a fixed body and drop the `error` that `read_for` returns, which is only handed back in `Proposal.reader_error`. Second, in run/mod.rs, `go_job`'s Proposed/no-reading arm (lines 331-333) bails. RealSteps::read turns that bail into `Read { job: None, error }`, so the drain's second attempt counts a second failure and `attempts` (drain.rs lines 1300-1302) ends `ItemEnd::Failed`, which sets RepeatedFailure. The plan's fixes match those spots. A new `read_unread` path uses the job's `next_seq`/`spent_usd`, as `correct` already does. A new `RunStep::Unread` branch is restricted to `ReadOf::Queued`, `!pre_read`, with both a job and an error. An unread counter is kept apart from `failures`, and a new `ItemEnd::Skipped` sets no stop. Together these fix the cause rather than the log line, and leave RepeatedFailure unchanged for jobs that were read. The test seams exist: `real_steps_with` (tests/drain.rs:2208), `rated_scenario` (:3253), `RecordingLander` (:1335), `common::Lines`, `Fixture::athena(script)`, a public `FakeTurn.structured`, and `Tweak`/`athena_with` in run_pin_tests.rs. The error text 'the reader returned no structured reading' (reading.rs:495) comes back as an error value, not an `Err`, so `first_reading` still commits. Choosing no-structured-output over a refused reading, so that 'exactly twice' means one drain re-read, is sound reasoning. Each demonstration would fail without the behavior it covers. I have only minor points; none blocks the plan.
